Description: Generation of new infections from existing infectious individuals. The number of new infections is modelled as the product of the time-varying reproduction number (R_t) with a discrete convolution of the previous infections, weighted by the serial interval distribution.

Name: R_t
Description: Time-varying reproduction number, modelled as a piecewise constant function that changes when an intervention occurs.

Name: Initial R_t
Description: Initial reproduction number before interventions, averaged across all countries (95% credible interval: 2.4–5.6).

Name: Serial Interval Distribution
Description: Distribution of the time between successive cases in a chain of transmission. Used to approximate the generation time distribution.

Name: Infection Fatality Ratio
Description: Population-averaged infection fatality ratio, adjusted for the age structure and contact patterns of each country. Based on previous work.

Name: Infection-to-death distribution
Description: Time lag distribution from infection to death, derived from assumptions about infection-to-symptom and symptom-to-death distributions.

Name: Lockdown effect
Description: The relative reduction in the reproduction number attributed to a lockdown intervention (95% credible interval: 75-87%).
